title: Association between the gut microbiota and hematopoietic stem cell mobilization in healthy donors
summary:
Stem cell donation involves collecting cells that can produce new blood cells. Before donation, donors receive a medicine that helps these cells move from inside the bones into the blood. The number of cells available in the blood after this preparation varies considerably between people. The reasons for these differences are not fully understood.

This study investigates whether the types and amounts of bacteria living in the gut are related to the number of these cells in the blood.

Up to 300 healthy donors will provide one stool sample before starting the medicine. The samples will be examined in a laboratory using the bacteria’s genetic material to identify which bacteria are present and their relative amounts. The number of blood-forming cells in the blood will be measured immediately before donation as part of the usual examinations. The usual preparation and donation procedures will remain unchanged.
conditions: Variability in hematopoietic stem cell mobilization in healthy donors

interventions.name:
Arm 1: Healthy hematopoietic stem cell donors with a low mobilization response, defined as a peripheral blood CD34+ cell concentration of <30 cells/µL immediately before stem cell apheresis.

A single stool sample is collected before the start of G-CSF mobilization to characterize the composition

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Healthy stem cell donors who are medically cleared for stem cell donation following mobilization with granulocyte colony-stimulating factor (G-CSF) and provide informed consent to participate in the study.
Exclusion criteria:
Cancellation of the planned G-CSF-mobilized stem cell donation despite prior medical clearance. Medical clearance exclusively for other types of donation. Absence of medical clearance for stem cell donation.
